speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. Can you describe the nature of your headache and specify which eye or eyes are experiencing the vision changes?

speaker: Patient
text: 69-year-old woman. The patient reports a 3-week history of headache and progressively worsening vision. She has not noticed any other symptoms, including no recent weight changes, no fevers, no night sweats, and no pain elsewhere in the body.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that information. Does the headache feel like it is located on one side of your head, and have you noticed any tenderness when you touch your scalp or temples?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Headache. I also have Worsening vision over the past 3 weeks, No weight changes, No fevers, No night sweats, No other pain.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you experience any jaw pain or difficulty chewing, particularly when eating tough foods? I also need to know if you have noticed any scalp tenderness or sensitivity when combing your hair.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: The patient has hypertension, which is controlled with medication. She also has a history of high cholesterol. Social history: Retired school teacher. Non-smoker and drinks alcohol socially. No recreational drug use.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you have any jaw claudication or scalp tenderness? I will also request an ESR and CRP to check for inflammation. REQUEST TEST: ESR REQUEST TEST: CRP

speaker: Doctor
text: The normal inflammatory markers make Giant Cell Arteritis less likely, so I need to investigate other causes for your headache and vision loss. Have you noticed any double vision, drooping eyelids, or weakness in your facial muscles?

speaker: Patient
text: Denies nausea, vomiting, diarrhea. No recent travel or sick contacts. No changes in hearing. Denies neck stiffness or photophobia.

speaker: Doctor
text: Since inflammatory markers are normal and you have vascular risk factors, I need to rule out a posterior reversible encephalopathy syndrome or other vascular causes. I will request an MRI of the brain to evaluate for structural or vascular abnormalities. REQUEST TEST: MRI_Brain

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: MRI_Brain: No acute intracranial abnormalities, no evidence of posterior reversible encephalopathy syndrome, no masses or vascular malformations identified.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the normal brain MRI and inflammatory markers, I need to focus on the optic nerve and orbital structures. I will request an MRI of the orbits to check for optic neuritis or compressive lesions. REQUEST TEST: MRI_Orbits

speaker: Doctor
text: Since the MRI of the orbits is normal, I need to evaluate the back of your eyes directly. I will now perform a dilated fundoscopic examination to look for signs of papilledema or other optic nerve abnormalities.

speaker: Patient
text: Denies nausea, vomiting, diarrhea. No recent travel or sick contacts. No changes in hearing. Denies neck stiffness or photophobia.

speaker: Doctor
text: What did you find during the dilated fundoscopic examination? REQUEST TEST: Fundoscopy

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Findings suggestive of retinal vein occlusion or hemorrhages.

speaker: Doctor
text: The fundoscopic findings of hemorrhages in a 69-year-old with headache and vision loss strongly suggest a vascular etiology affecting the retina. DIAGNOSIS READY: Central Retinal Vein Occlusion
